mechanism_narrative: The three-week improvement in TRANSIT from -38.1 to -29.1 signals restored out-of-home mobility, which raises footfall in retail-and-recreation venues over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -38.1 at t-3w to -29.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days when TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points over three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -20%, it marks a policy-enabled return to workplaces that increases weekday retail-and-recreation spending over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20% after being below -20% in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES crossed -20 at t-1w and stayed above at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed its last 14-day mean after WORKPLACES crosses above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high PARKS activity and recovering TRANSIT indicate a broad outdoor-leisure re-engagement that spills into retail-and-recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 16.6 and TRANSIT was -29.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS > 15 and TRANSIT > -30, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not greater than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-holiday reopening regime, a decline in RESIDENTIAL from 9.4 to 6.6 shows people leaving home for seasonal leisure, which drives RETAIL_REC up over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.4 at t-3w to 6.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: In the post-holiday reopening regime, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its last 7-day mean when RESIDENTIAL declines.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GROCERY_PHARM readings for two consecutive weeks signal essential-goods stockpiling under health policy advisories, diverting spending from retail-and-recreation and lowering RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 4.6 at t-1w and 1.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is greater than or equal to its last 14-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM is positive for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: High PARKS activity combined with elevated RESIDENTIAL reflects substitution of outdoor recreation for indoor retail-and-recreation trips, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 16.6 and RESIDENTIAL was 6.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS > 15 and RESIDENTIAL > 5, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than its last 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remaining below -25% for two consecutive weeks signals continued transit-aversion and restricted access to dense retail districts, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -28.4 at t-1w and -29.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT stays below -25% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL marks a return-to-office shift that expands weekday retail-and-recreation activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -19.6 to -16.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.4 to 6.6
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls over four weeks, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not greater than its last 28-day mean.
